bullets.title: MRVL: Citi raises PT to $275 on landmark Google XPU deal; FY28E EPS 26% above Street
bullets.body: Citi raises MRVL PT to $275 (from prior) and lifts FY27E/FY28E EPS 6%/26% above Street ahead of Aug 27 earnings, driven by expanded Google commercial agreement through FY2033 covering AI inference accelerators, networking, storage controllers, and near-memory compute. Google issued 58.9M share warrant worth up to $12.2B (vesting per $500M in eligible custom-product revenue tranches), potentially representing ~$120B in revenue. Citi views this as an LPU (not TPU) ramp in 2028, structurally diversifying MRVL away from Amazon; maintains Buy.

bullets.title: BABA: Q1 EPS miss on AI capex surge; JPM maintains OW $205 PT, sees dip-buy opportunity
bullets.body: Alibaba Q1 non-GAAP EPS CNY8.52 missed consensus by ~18-24% as capex surged 75% YoY to CNY67.7B and net income dropped 76%; revenue of CNY268.95B narrowly beat. AI Cloud revenue accelerated +45% YoY to CNY48.4B with EBITA +133% and 11.6% margin. JPM maintains OW ($205 US / HK$200) at 16x FY28E P/E, targeting $10B AI product ARR next quarter and $100B cloud revenue by 2030; ADRs initially fell ~4-5% before recovering ~0.5% intraday.

bullets.title: CRWD: CTO Zaitsev departure weighs -2-3% premarket; DADCO reiterates Buy, $191 PT
bullets.body: CrowdStrike CTO Elia Zaitsev is departing after 13 years to launch Cognition, an agentic AI security venture fund targeting $170M. DADCO reiterates Buy ($191 PT) and expects CRWD to deliver more typical ARR upside in Q2 vs. the lighter Q1 beat; notes CRWD is dominating alongside PANW and has outperformed IGV by 76% YTD, though trades at ~79x FCF vs. 20-30%+ growth peers at ~39x. Stock was -2 to -3% premarket.

bullets.title: NVDA: Earnings Aug 26 is key catalyst; Hedgeye expects beat with better guidance
bullets.body: NVDA reports Aug 26, with Jackson Hole (Warsh speaks Aug 28) and PCE also that week. Hedgeye expects NVDA to beat with somewhat better guidance; key variables are magnitude of guidance raise and incremental AI infrastructure order growth. JPM's Harlan Sur hosting AMA on NVDA/SNPS/MRVL on Aug 28; Wolfe's Chris Caso covering NVDA/AVGO/MRVL implications Aug 21.

bullets.title: OKTA: DADCO raises PT to $165, expects ~13%+ CRPO growth in FQ2 and re-rating
bullets.body: DA Davidson raises OKTA PT from $130 to $165 (27.5x FCF vs. mid-teens growth peers at ~20x), citing VAR survey showing net sales performance up Q/Q for second straight quarter and improving sales morale/productivity. Expects ~13%+ Y/Y FQ2 CRPO growth (vs. +12% prior) and guides FQ3 acceleration to ~14% Y/Y. IGA contribution and early AI agent traction highlighted. OKTA has outperformed IGV by 69% YTD.

bullets.title: DKNG: NY OSB GGR +38% Y/Y week of 8/16; 3QTD share holding at 35%
bullets.body: NY OSB total GGR +34% Y/Y for the week ending Aug 16, with DraftKings at +38% GGR (+14% handle) and 3QTD GGR tracking +33% Y/Y. DraftKings 3QTD GGR share 35% vs. 34% PY, while FanDuel slipped to 39% from 41%. Total hold rate 11.7% (+440bps Y/Y) on the week. JPM hosting G2E investor meetings with DKNG CFO Alan Ellingson Sept 29.

bullets.title: NBIS: $5B convertible offering triggers -12% sell-off; 22V long on AI compute thesis
bullets.body: Nebius Group (NBIS) priced $3B and $2B in convertibles (total $5B), sending shares down ~12% on dilution. Despite the drawdown, 22V Research maintains NBIS as highest-conviction AI infrastructure long alongside CRWV, targeting compute and liquid cooling plays (ECL, ETN, JCI). JPM's morning note also flagged NBIS capital raise as notable.

bullets.title: SHOP & AMZN: JPM raises US e-comm growth to +9.7%; both remain Best Ideas
bullets.body: JPM upgrades 2026 US e-commerce growth forecast to +9.7% after 2Q accelerated to +12.4% Y/Y. AMZN's US share rose to ~48% (+130bps Y/Y) while SHOP powered ~16% of US e-commerce (+190bps Y/Y), growing 2.5-3x faster than the broader market. JPM projects SHOP US GMV ex-POS +25% in 3Q and +26% for 2026; sees SHOP powering 20%+ of US e-commerce by 2028. Rosenblatt also initiates SHOP Buy at $175.

bullets.title: NTES: JPM reiterates OW; Q2 game revenue +10% Y/Y despite headline EPS miss on PDD loss
bullets.body: NetEase Q2 net profit missed ~24% due to a Rmb3B investment loss tied to a 25% decline in PDD holdings; stripping that out, operating profit beat JPM estimates by 6% at Rmb12.9B. Online game revenue accelerated to +10% Y/Y (from +7% in 1Q), Game & VAS GPM improved to 76.1% (+5.9ppts YoY), and ANANTA launching 3Q26 is projected to generate Rmb12B in its first 12 months. JPM PT HK$290 / $185 USD (OW) at 20x 2026E P/E; stock fell ~4% premarket on headline miss.

bullets.title: CRM: Oppenheimer bullish into Aug 26 print; F2Q CRPO +15% Y/Y expected, F3Q guide is binary catalyst
bullets.body: Oppenheimer is bullish on Salesforce ahead of F2Q earnings (Aug 26), expecting CRPO of $33.8B+ (+15% Y/Y, ~200bps above consensus). The F3Q CRPO guide is the key binary: 13-14% Y/Y growth is well-received, below 13% disappoints. Agentforce AI ramping with strong deal wins but adoption slower than expected. Investor Day next month provides additional catalyst.

bullets.title: INTU: Earnings Aug 25; consensus $4.27B revenue (+11.4%), $3.58 EPS; 10.3% move implied
bullets.body: StreetAccount consensus for INTU Q4 (reports Aug 25) is $4.27B revenue (+11.4% Y/Y, in-line with company +11-12% guidance) and $3.58 EPS. Stock is +5.6% since May vs. S&P +3.7%. INTU has beaten EPS in 19 of last 20 quarters; near-term options imply ~10.3% post-earnings move.

bullets.title: TRI: UBS reiterates Buy, $140 PT; CoCounsel AI enhancements reinforce legal data moat
bullets.body: UBS reiterates Buy on Thomson Reuters (TRI) with $140 PT (~17x 2028E EBITDA), highlighting CoCounsel Legal's new AI capabilities including Westlaw Brief Builder, Drafting Agent, and Deep Research Verify via Anthropic's Claude. Stock is -20% YTD despite 35%+ recovery from June lows and a Q2 raise in 2026 Big 3 organic growth guide to +9.5-10%. UBS argues proprietary legal datasets are difficult to replicate.

bullets.title: SPHR: Piper Sandler initiates Overweight, $185 PT on Vegas demand and Sphere expansion
bullets.body: Piper Sandler initiates SPHR at Overweight with a $185 price target, citing achievable 2027 Vegas demand expectations, strong in-person experience tailwinds, and upside from future Sphere venues with margin benefits. MSGE initiated at Neutral ($86 PT) as recent strength is largely in the valuation.

bullets.title: META: Faces six-week CA trial with $200B penalty risk; quietly one of MSFT's largest AI customers
bullets.body: Meta's California trial over alleged social media harms to children begins, with state AGs claiming $200B in civil penalties and restitution; Meta warned $1.4T damages would be existential. Separately, Meta has emerged as one of Microsoft's largest AI customers, reportedly spending hundreds of millions annually on Azure AI, representing a significant concentration for MSFT's AI revenue (OAI ~70%, META a major portion).

bullets.title: GOOGL vs. NFLX creator battle; Conduent/Google Cloud eDiscovery AI partnership
bullets.body: YouTube is offering millions to creators for exclusivity against Netflix content deals, threatening marketing and feature reductions for dual-platform creators. Separately, Conduent partnered with Google Cloud to integrate Gemini models into its Viewpoint eDiscovery platform. Rosenblatt also upgraded GOOGL to Buy (from Neutral), raising PT to $410 from $393.

bullets.title: EQIX: MS constructive on data center moat; open-weight AI adoption seen tilting demand toward EQIX
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley's Cameron McVeigh is constructive on Equinix, noting interconnection scale as the key competitive moat and arguing open-weight AI adoption should tilt enterprise demand toward EQIX vs. hyperscaler-captive facilities. Barclays upgraded AMT and CCI to Overweight; data center development costs running $11-13M+/MW with 8%+ yields in emerging markets like North Dakota.

bullets.title: RCL: Positioned as 'screaming buy' after VIK print on white-hot Ocean pricing
bullets.body: After Viking (VIK) Q2 beat—with 2026 pricing re-accelerating to +6% and 2027 Ocean pricing up 10%—the analyst calls RCL a screaming buy, citing the white-hot Ocean pricing backdrop. VIK Q3 EBITDA impact from River cancellations raised to $50-70M; VIK Best Idea Long at $120 NTM PT (+30% upside) but RCL flagged as the tactical near-term trade.

bullets.title: BOX: Earnings Aug 25; consensus $319.3M revenue, $0.40 EPS; options imply ~11.5% move
bullets.body: StreetAccount consensus for BOX Q2 (reports Aug 25) is revenue $319.3M (vs. $319M guidance) and non-GAAP EPS $0.40 (vs. ~$0.39 guide). BOX stock is +29.3% since late May vs. S&P +2.5%. Revenue beaten in 16 of last 20 quarters; near-term options imply ~11.5% post-earnings move. Short interest at 12%.

bullets.title: Mag-7/AI momentum unwind: High-beta momentum -7% in two days; hyperscalers resilient
bullets.body: Tech Momentum factor fell ~18% over two days driven by quant/systematic de-risking and Anthropic ARR underwhelm ($65B); S&P closed +21bps masking a Momentum drawdown of ~5%. Hyperscalers saw median institutional share holdings actually rise +2.7% in 2Q despite the AI ROI debate. 22V and JPM both note the pullback is creating selective entry points in AI infrastructure (CRWV, NBIS, liquid cooling).

bullets.title: WRBY: AI glasses launch seen as near-term catalyst; Hedgeye bullish alongside Google/Samsung
bullets.body: Hedgeye highlights Warby Parker as a key beneficiary of the approaching AI glasses launch cycle, positioned alongside Google and Samsung. The standalone core business is also viewed as attractive. WRBY surged on an AI email catalyst per Hedgeye's daily note.
